Pitbull story

By: Tarryn Crossman | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
The Sizwe Kupelo foundation (spokesperson for the EC DOH) has caused a storm recently with a petition to castrate male Pitbull’s, sterilize the females and ban Pitbull’s as domestic pets, following a series of serious attacks over the past year.

Since they announced the petition Pitbull attacks around the country have been making headlines on the weekly, resulting in widespread panic from Pitbull owners, as well as the community.
But this is a complex story with horrific sadness on both sides.
1. Henneman
3-year-old toddler was mauled and killed by two Pitbull’s, the dogs and owner were then attacked by the community. The one dog was killed with a spade and then both dogs were burnt. The owner was removed to a place of safety by the SAPS.
This is story is a good case study, because both the loss of the child and the conditions that the dogs were kept in is tragic. They were caged and chained and basically just existed to breed. For this power breed, that was breed to fight, that is a recipe for disaster.
2. Case study 2 – Gauteng

Tshego, a mom of three was attacked on the back of her head when a Pitbull was roaming the streets near her home. Tshego was left with 27 stitches in the back of head, and now suffers from PTSD, memory loss and migraines.
The 23-year-old owner of the dog apologized and said he had given the dog to the SPCA. But he never did, instead he moved to another house further down the street. They a are male and female breading pair.
Jerry from Soweto animal rescue and advisory board, has the legal authority to remove a dog that has attacked a human. He is willing to do this removal with us on camera

Jerry is a good specialist; he is adamant that these dogs can be rehabilitated. He is Pitbull’s handed over to them on the weekly now. He says that the owners are afraid of the dogs now and of the community taking action against them


Further information:
Specialists
Pitbull federation – great specialist for understanding the breed, its genetic history and why you can’t blame the whole breed.
They are calling for stricter regulations on breeding and owning a power breed
“At the moment we only have the laws that govern in the instances of pitbull bites or if there is a mauling or a death. Then we have laws that govern that situation which make criminal case. But in terms of owning a power breed and breeding such dogs, there is no legislation and that is one of the things that the Pitbull Federation is trying to push at government level,” Lins Rheeder
The federation is so clear that no amount of love can remove the aggressive genetic predisposition of this breed, it has to be trained and controlled and you have always have be aware of the dog you own, and the potential threat it offers.
Sandra swart – she is a historian who specialises on dogs in society – we may jusy be able to do what she has to say in VO
But it is interesting to understand genetically where this dog comes from, from an expert, and also the history of other dogs that were banned or seen as a threat in history.
NSPCA - LEGAL

Script:


It was Sunday morning like any other in the Free state town of Hennaman
3-year-old Keketso Saule had woken up early and was playing with his school friends only a few meters from where he lived with his grandfather Lukas SAULE


The attack was horrific. This video shows bystanders watching helplessly. Within minutes Keketso was dead

This is one of many horrific pit bull attacks in the last year. Now, more and more South Africans are calling for a ban on this power breed, that was bred for dog fighting


Leigh Shenker, a lecturer at the international Centre for Applied Pet Ethology or CoAPE, is an animal behaviorist specializing in pit bulls

According to the neighbours, the two pit bulls that attacked Keketso were being used FOR security… almost permanently chained up in these two cages…BUT on that fatal day, the owner allegedly left the gate open… and they escaped.

Tshego Molopo was walking her dog near her home in Kagiso, Krugersdorp when a random pitbull roaming the streets attacked her.

The owner of the dog arrived and managed to remove his Pit bull, Tshego survived …BUT with 17 stitches to the back of her head

We contacted Jerry Selwane from Soweto Animal Rescue and informed him of the delays in the case… in less than a week he obtained a warrant to inspect the property and try confiscate the dog that attacked Tshego,

When we arrived at the owner’s home.
I was horrified to see the condition of a dog in his backyard

Tsegho was adamant that THIS WAS NOT the DOG that attacked her. According to the owner he HAD surrendered that dog to the SPCA

Unlicensed breeding is legal in South Africa. ONLY the Eastern and Western Cape provinces have by-laws regulating that female dogs have to be spayed… or the owner has to register as a breeder. With backstreet-bred Pitbulls fetching anything between 200 and 1500 rand, it’s a lucrative business.

Lehanda Rheeder is the spokesperson for the pit bull federation of south africa, who represent over 1500 pitbull owners

Back in Kagiso the owner of the pitbull that attacked Tsego was taking us on a wild goose chase. At one house we were told that the dog was dead, yet the owner was adamant that he had taken it to the SPCA, eventually Selwane called off the search, and even though the Animal Protection Act states that the owner is liable, and can be sentenced to a fine or up to two years in jail, he was escorted home… to date he has not been charged and the dog has not been located

This isn’t an isolated case… South Africans are afraid, and taking it out on Pit bulls, or dogs that are suspected to be pit bulls, Innocent or not. As a result, many owners are trying to surrender their pets to the SPCA or rescue centres like Dani Gudwulfs pit bull rescue

Of the 70 Pit bulls at the not-for-profit organisation Gudwulfs, many have been rescued from dog fighting rings or drug houses. Through consistent training, Gudwulf believes they have been socialized.
End VO on Dan in Ivans cage


Keshvi Nair is the public relations officer at the NSPCA.

In Keketso’s case, the owner has been charged with culpable homicide and is currently out on bail awaiting trial.

The NSPCA is just one of several stakeholders working on a plan to stop these deadly dog attacks, but ultimately a legislated change has to come from the department of agriculture, land reform and rural development, and while the debate rages, attacks continue.


But, if a solution is ever found, it'll be too late for families like the Saules.
